objectives.text: Amend FINRA Rule 3310 to conform to FinCEN's CDD Rule and aid member firms in complying with the CDD Rule's requirements by incorporating the ongoing customer due diligence requirement into the rule.

citations.quote: The recently filed amendments to FINRA Rule 3310 incorporate into the rule this ongoing customer due diligence requirement to conform the rule to the CDD Rule and aid member firms in complying with the CDD Rule's requirements.

obligations.action: Develop and implement a written anti-money laundering program reasonably designed to achieve and monitor the member's compliance with the requirements of the Bank Secrecy Act and the implementing regulations promulgated thereunder by the Department of the Treasury.

citations.quote: Each member shall develop and implement a written anti-money laundering program reasonably designed to achieve and monitor the member's compliance with the requirements of the Bank Secrecy Act (31 U.S.C. 5311, et seq.), and the implementing regulations promulgated thereunder by the Department of the Treasury.

obligations.action: Be approved, in writing, by a member of senior management.

citations.quote: Each member's anti-money laundering program must be approved, in writing, by a member of senior management.

obligations.action: Designate and identify to FINRA (by name, title, mailing address, e-mail address, telephone number, and facsimile number) an individual or individuals responsible for implementing and monitoring the day-to-day operations and internal controls of the program (such individual or individuals must be an associated person of the member) and provide prompt notification to FINRA regarding any change in such designation(s).

citations.quote: Designate and identify to FINRA (by name, title, mailing address, e-mail address, telephone number, and facsimile number) an individual or individuals responsible for implementing and monitoring the day-to-day operations and internal controls of the program
such individual or individuals must be an associated person of the member) and provide prompt notification to FINRA regarding any change in such designation(s)

obligations.action: Provide ongoing training for appropriate personnel.

citations.quote: Provide ongoing training for appropriate personnel

obligations.action: Include appropriate risk-based procedures for conducting ongoing customer due diligence, to include, but not be limited to: understanding the nature and purpose of customer relationships for the purpose of developing a customer risk profile; and conducting ongoing monitoring to identify and report suspicious transactions and, on a risk basis, to maintain and update customer information.

citations.quote:
Include appropriate risk-based procedures for conducting ongoing customer due diligence, to include, but not be limited to:
 
 (i) Understanding the nature and purpose of customer relationships for the purpose of developing a customer risk profile; and

(ii) Conducting ongoing monitoring to identify and report suspicious transactions and, on a risk basis, to maintain and update customer information. For purposes of paragraph (f)(ii), customer information shall include information regarding the beneficial owners of legal entity customers (as defined in 31 CFR 1010.230(e)).

obligations.action: Ensure that their AML programs are updated, as necessary, to comply with the CDD Rule by May 11, 2018.

citations.quote: Member firms should ensure that their AML programs are updated, as necessary, to comply with the CDD Rule by May 11, 2018.

definitions.definition: The Financial Crimes Enforcement Network's (FinCEN) final rule on Customer Due Diligence Requirements for Financial Institutions; issued May 11, 2016 to clarify and strengthen customer due diligence for covered financial institutions, including broker-dealers.

citations.quote: FinCEN, the bureau of the Department of the Treasury responsible for administering the Bank Secrecy Act2 (BSA) and its implementing regulations, issued the CDD Rule3 to clarify and strengthen customer due diligence for covered financial institutions,4 including broker-dealers.

definitions.definition: FinCEN identifies four components of customer due diligence: (1) customer identification and verification; (2) beneficial ownership identification and verification; (3) understanding the nature and purpose of customer relationships; and (4) ongoing monitoring for reporting suspicious transactions and, on a risk basis, maintaining and updating customer information.

citations.quote: In its CDD Rule, FinCEN identifies four components of customer due diligence: (1) customer identification and verification; (2) beneficial ownership identification and verification; (3) understanding the nature and purpose of customer relationships; and (4) ongoing monitoring for reporting suspicious transactions and, on a risk basis, maintaining and updating customer information.

definitions.definition: The requirement, added by the CDD Rule amending the existing AML program rules for covered financial institutions, to explicitly include the third and fourth CDD components (understanding the nature and purpose of customer relationships; and ongoing monitoring) in AML programs.

citations.quote: The CDD Rule also addresses the third and fourth components by amending the existing AML program rules for covered financial institutions to explicitly require these components to be included in AML programs as a new "fifth pillar."

interactions.description: FINRA Rule 3310 is amended to conform to FinCEN's CDD Rule, which was adopted under the Bank Secrecy Act and its implementing regulations administered by FinCEN.
references: Bank Secrecy Act (31 U.S.C. 5311, et seq.)

citations.quote: FINRA has filed for immediate effectiveness amendments to FINRA Rule 3310 (Anti-Money Laundering Compliance Program) to reflect the Financial Crimes Enforcement Network's (FinCEN) adoption of a final rule on Customer Due Diligence Requirements for Financial Institutions (CDD Rule).

interactions.description: FinCEN's authority to impose AML program requirements and require compliance procedures derives from 31 U.S.C. 5318(h)(2) and (a)(2).

citations.quote: FinCEN is authorized to impose AML program requirements on financial institutions and to require financial institutions to maintain procedures to ensure compliance with the BSA and associated regulations. 31 U.S.C. 5318(h)(2) and (a)(2).

interactions.description: The CDD Rule Release is published at 81 FR 29397 (May 11, 2016), with technical correcting amendments at 82 FR 45182 (September 28, 2017); the rulemaking originated with 77 FR 13046 (ANPR) and 79 FR 45151 (NPRM).

citations.quote: FinCEN Customer Due Diligence Requirements for Financial Institutions; CDD Rule, 81 FR 29397 (May 11, 2016) (CDD Rule Release); 82 FR 45182 (September 28, 2017) (making technical correcting amendments to the final CDD Rule published on May 11, 2016).

interactions.description: FINRA previously published Regulatory Notice 17-40 to provide guidance to member firms regarding their obligations under FINRA Rule 3310 in light of the CDD Rule, including the 'fifth pillar' requirement.

citations.quote: On November 21, 2017, FINRA published Regulatory Notice 17-40 to provide guidance to member firms regarding their obligations under FINRA Rule 3310 in light of the adoption of FinCEN's CDD Rule.

interactions.description: The amendments were filed for immediate effectiveness with the SEC via Securities Exchange Act Release No. 83154 (File No. SR-FINRA-2018-016).

citations.quote: See Securities Exchange Act Release No. 83154 (May 2, 2018) (Notice of Filing and Immediate Effectiveness File No. SR-FINRA-2018-016).

notes: This is a FINRA Regulatory Notice (sro_guidance) announcing rule amendments; Attachment A reproduces the amended text of FINRA Rule 3310 with paragraphs (a) through (c) marked 'No change' and thus not reproduced here — their substantive content is unavailable in this source. The rule text uses 'shall' for the general program obligations (extracted as must) and 'must' for the senior-management approval and associated-person requirements. The Notice states the CDD provisions 'are not new and merely codify existing expectations,' an interpretive characterization preserved as written. OBL-6 uses 'should' in the Notice's hortatory guidance, distinct from the rule's mandatory 'shall/must' text. OBL-3's citation was split into two verbatim spans to stay within length limits.
